requirement: Load service settings from environment variables with validation and defaults, plus a test helper that runs a block with exactly the given variables and restores the environment afterwards.
skeleton: Frozen ServiceConfig dataclass, load_config reading and validating three SERVICE_ variables, and isolated_env contextmanager wrapping patch.dict on os.environ with clear=True.
caption: Environment-driven configuration tested with unittest.mock.patch.dict. ServiceConfig is a frozen dataclass with url, workers defaulting to 4 and debug defaulting to False. load_config() reads os.environ: SERVICE_URL is stripped and a missing or blank value raises LookupError saying SERVICE_URL is not set; SERVICE_WORKERS is parsed with int, defaulting to 4, and a value below 1 raises ValueError saying SERVICE_WORKERS must be at least 1 with the value it got; SERVICE_DEBUG is true only when its stripped, lowercased value is 1, true or yes. isolated_env(**values) is a contextlib.contextmanager wrapping patch.dict(os.environ, values, clear=True), so inside the block the process environment holds exactly the given variables, and on exit patch.dict restores every original variable and removes the added ones, even if the block raised. The fixture asserts that a padded URL, eight workers and debug Yes load as ServiceConfig('http://svc', 8, True), that defaults give four workers and no debug, that 0, no, empty and off are not debug, that a SERVICE_URL set outside the block does not leak in and LookupError is raised, that a blank URL raises LookupError, that zero workers raises ValueError, and that the outer SERVICE_URL comes back while SERVICE_WORKERS is removed after the block.

plan.intent: Test environment-based config without leaking variables
constraints: A missing or blank SERVICE_URL raises LookupError
SERVICE_WORKERS defaults to 4 and below 1 raises ValueError
SERVICE_DEBUG is true only for 1, true or yes in any case
Variables set outside the helper are invisible inside it
The original environment is restored after the block

rationale.teaches: patch.dict(os.environ, values, clear=True) as the isolation primitive for environment reads, restoring both changed and added keys.
rationale.why: Tests that write os.environ directly leak settings into later tests, and without clear the developer's own shell variables decide whether the test passes.

ops.docstring: Read service settings from os.environ and isolate them in tests with patch.dict.

candidates.why_wrong: Without clear the outer SERVICE_URL leaks into the isolated block.
The URL is not stripped, so padding is kept and a blank value passes.
Zero workers is accepted because only negatives are rejected.
The worker count defaults to 2 instead of 4.
os.environ.update never restores the environment, so values leak out of the block.
